Calibrate the sensible heat flux from the anchor pixels

Source: R/metric-sensible-heat.R
ef_calibrate_h.Rd

Internal calibration of METRIC: finds the coefficients of \(dT = a + b\,T_{s,datum}\) such that the hot and cold anchor pixels reproduce their target sensible heat flux \(H_{target} = R_n - G - LE_{target}\), iterating the aerodynamic resistance with the Monin-Obukhov stability correction (phase A), and optionally computes the sensible heat flux of every pixel with the calibrated coefficients (phase B, strategy P2).

Usage

ef_calibrate_h(anchors, control, lapse_rate, datum_elevation, pixels = NULL)

Arguments

anchors

The calibration points: a data.frame with exactly one row of type "hot" and one of type "cold" (one calibration point per anchor class, decision P0-9), or an earthflux_anchors object whose element calibration_points is such a data frame. Required columns (dev/specs/sensible-heat.md section 2.2):

  • type: "hot" or "cold";

  • lst: land surface temperature [K];

  • elevation: elevation [m];

  • zom: momentum roughness length [m] (see ef_zom());

  • rn: net radiation [W m-2];

  • g: soil heat flux [W m-2];

  • le_target: target latent heat flux of the anchor [W m-2] (its boundary condition, computed by the anchor module);

  • u_blend: wind speed at the blending height [m s-1] (see ef_blending_wind());

  • pressure: atmospheric pressure [kPa].

An optional column anchor_id is carried to the result; other columns are ignored. Missing values at an anchor raise earthflux_calibration_error.

control

The list returned by ef_h_control() (heights, the height of the stable momentum correction of decision SH-11 and the convergence settings), e.g. ef_h_control() for its defaults. It is validated again; elements not given take the defaults of ef_h_control().

lapse_rate

Numeric scalar. Lapse rate of the surface temperature with elevation [K m-1] (see ef_ts_datum()). No default (SH-13).

datum_elevation

Numeric scalar. Elevation of the temperature datum [m], a constant of the scene (see ef_ts_datum()).

pixels

NULL (phase A only) or a list (or data.frame) of numeric vectors, matrices or arrays of length 1 or a common length, with elements lst [K], elevation [m], zom [m], u_blend [m s-1] and pressure [kPa], and optionally rn and g [W m-2] (used only to diagnose EF_H_GT_AVAILABLE). Missing values propagate to the outputs of the pixel.

Value

An object of class earthflux_h_calibration, a list with:

  • a [K], b [-]: calibrated coefficients (a*, b*), obtained by solving the anchor conditions once more with the final \(r_{ah}\) (closure), so that the anchors reproduce \(H_{target}\) exactly;

  • converged (logical) and iterations (integer) of phase A;

  • trace: data.frame with one row per iteration: iteration, a, b (the iterate \(a_k, b_k\)), delta_a, delta_b, max_rel_change (convergence statistic) and, for each anchor (_hot, _cold), dt, air_density, obukhov_length, u_star and rah;

  • anchors: data.frame with the final state of each anchor (anchor_id, type, lst, elevation, ts_datum, h_target, dt, air_density, rah, u_star, obukhov_length, h);

  • pixels: NULL, or a list with h [W m-2], dt [K], ts_datum [K], air_density [kg m-3], rah [s m-1], u_star [m s-1], obukhov_length [m], converged (logical) and iterations (integer), each with the shape of the pixel inputs;

  • control, datum (lapse_rate, datum_elevation), constants (von_karman, gravity, cp and their status) and provenance;

  • flags: list of earthflux_flag records, one per code that holds somewhere: the object flags EF_H_CALIBRATION_NOT_CONVERGED and EF_H_DT_SLOPE_NONPOSITIVE (both critical), and, with pixels, the cell flags EF_H_USTAR_INVALID, EF_H_PIXEL_NOT_CONVERGED, EF_H_DT_EXTRAPOLATED_HOT, EF_H_DT_EXTRAPOLATED_COLD, EF_H_NEGATIVE and (with rn and g) EF_H_GT_AVAILABLE. A code evaluated but absent has no record; the codes evaluated are listed in provenance$flags_evaluated.

Details

Phase A (anchors). Start (k = 0): neutral \(u_*\) and \(r_{ah}\) (see ef_ustar(), ef_rah()) and \(dT_0 = 0\) (SH-19). At each iteration k:

  1. \(\rho_k\) with ef_air_density() at \(T_a = T_s - dT_{k-1}\) (SH-08);

  2. \(dT_k = H_{target} r_{ah,k-1} / (\rho_k c_p)\) at each anchor;

  3. \(a_k, b_k\) with ef_dt_coef();

  4. \(H_k = \rho_k c_p (a_k + b_k T_{s,datum}) / r_{ah,k-1}\) (equal to the target by construction);

  5. Monin-Obukhov length \(L = -\rho c_p u_*^3 T_s / (k g H)\) with \(u_{*,k-1}\), the surface temperature \(T_s\) and \(\rho_k\) (Waters et al., 2002, Eq. 34; SH-10; \(L = \infty\), neutral, when \(H = 0\));

  6. stability corrections (unstable: Paulson-type forms with coefficient 16; stable: log-linear form \(-5 z/L\)), with \(\psi_m\) at the blending height (or at stable_psi_m_height when \(L > 0\): 2 m by default, Waters et al., 2002, Eq. 38, decision SH-11) and \(\psi_h\) at z2 and z1; then \(u_{*,k}\) and the new \(r_{ah}\);

  7. damping: \(r_{ah,k} = (1 - \omega) r_{ah,new} + \omega r_{ah,k-1}\);

  8. convergence when \(\max_i |r_{ah,k} - r_{ah,k-1}| / r_{ah,k} < tol\) over both anchors.

Closure: steps 1-3 are repeated with the final \(r_{ah}\) to give (a*, b*), and \(r_{ah}\) is not updated afterwards, so the anchors reproduce \(H_{target}\) exactly.

Phase B (pixels, strategy P2, decision P0-10). With (a*, b*) fixed, \(dT = a^* + b^* T_{s,datum}\) and \(\rho\) (at \(T_a = T_s - dT\)) are fixed; each pixel iterates only its stability correction (\(H \to L \to \psi \to u_* \to r_{ah}\)) from the neutral state until its own convergence (same tol, maxit and damping). The result of a pixel depends only on its inputs and on (a*, b*), not on the other pixels nor on the path of phase A, so the computation can be split into blocks.

Failures are never silent.

  • Phase A without convergence after maxit iterations: the last iterate is returned with converged = FALSE, a warning of class earthflux_convergence_warning is signalled (fields iterations and trace) and the object flag EF_H_CALIBRATION_NOT_CONVERGED (critical) is set.

  • Calibrated slope b <= 0: a warning of class earthflux_warning and the object flag EF_H_DT_SLOPE_NONPOSITIVE (critical).

  • Missing values at an anchor, u_blend = 0 at an anchor, datum temperature of the hot anchor not greater than that of the cold anchor, or non-finite \(a\), \(b\), \(u_*\), \(r_{ah}\) or air density at an anchor during the iteration: error of class earthflux_calibration_error (fields iteration and trace when the failure occurs during the iteration).

  • A pixel whose friction velocity becomes undefined (see ef_ustar()) or not positive: NA outputs for that pixel and the cell flag EF_H_USTAR_INVALID; a pixel without convergence keeps its last iterate and gets EF_H_PIXEL_NOT_CONVERGED.

Constants: von Karman constant EF_VON_KARMAN (0.41), gravity EF_GRAVITY (9.81 m s-2) and specific heat of air EF_SPECIFIC_HEAT_AIR (1004 J kg-1 K-1), the values of Waters et al. (2002, pp. 25-26 and 32); they are recorded in constants.

Verification status: the forms are VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): the iterative scheme of Waters et al. (2002), pp. 25-34 (figure 4, Eqs. 25-41) and appendix 8 (anchor conditions of p. 30-31, dT from Eq. 33, \(dT\) linear in the surface temperature, Eq. 32, Monin-Obukhov length with \(T_s\), Eq. 34, stability corrections, Eqs. 35-39, corrected \(u_*\) and \(r_{ah}\), Eqs. 40-41). The procedural choices are EarthFlux decisions (P0-10, CANDIDATA as procedure): the manual iterates "until the successive values for dT_hot and rah at the hot pixel have stabilized" (p. 34; 3 to 7 iterations, appendix 8), whereas EarthFlux uses a relative tolerance on rah at both anchors, the closure of the anchors and phase B with the per-pixel strategy P2. Known differences with water are listed in section 17 of dev/specs/sensible-heat.md (e.g. no wind floor, no substitute friction velocity, per-anchor convergence, strategy P2). The cross-check with Allen, Tasumi and Trezza (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking; Paulson (1970) and Webb (1970) were not consulted.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

Paulson, C. A. (1970). The mathematical representation of wind speed and temperature profiles in the unstable atmospheric surface layer. Journal of Applied Meteorology, 9(6), 857-861. doi:10.1175/1520-0450(1970)009<0857:TMROWS>2.0.CO;2

Webb, E. K. (1970). Profile relationships: The log-linear range, and extension to strong stability. Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 96(407), 67-90. doi:10.1002/qj.49709640708

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_blending_wind(), ef_dt_coef(), ef_h_control(), ef_rah(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ts_datum(), ef_ustar(), ef_zom()

Examples

# Synthetic scene of dev/specs/sensible-heat.md section 14
u_b <- ef_blending_wind(3, height = 2, zom_station = 0.015, d_station = 0,
                        blending_height = 200)
anchors <- data.frame(
  type = c("cold", "hot"),
  lst = c(300, 316),
  elevation = c(500, 700),
  zom = c(0.06, 0.005),
  rn = c(600, 480),
  g = c(50, 110),
  le_target = c(520, 0),
  u_blend = u_b,
  pressure = ef_air_pressure(c(500, 700))
)
# Heights of the SEBAL Idaho manual (the defaults of ef_h_control())
ctrl <- ef_h_control()
cal <- ef_calibrate_h(anchors, control = ctrl, lapse_rate = 0.00649,
                      datum_elevation = 500,
                      pixels = list(lst = 308, elevation = 500, zom = 0.02,
                                    u_blend = u_b,
                                    pressure = ef_air_pressure(500)))
c(a = cal$a, b = cal$b, iterations = cal$iterations)
#>           a           b  iterations 
#> -87.4397761   0.2932606   6.0000000 
cal$pixels$h
#> [1] 182.3605
